notes: One canonical question per ask, shared by Skill 49 (launch and legacy), Skill 71, Skill 83. Same questions and same answers file in claude-nine, Claude Code and OpenClaw; only the rendering differs. choices has at most 3 entries; the renderer always adds the help_label option. never_default questions are never defaulted; every other question may fall back to its default, flagged 'to confirm'.

system_fields.schema_version: set by the launch record writer
system_fields.offers: built from offer_name, price, deliverables, extras
system_fields.extras: built from bump, upsell_1, downsell_1, upsell_2, downsell_2
system_fields.brand_ref: path of the brand file generated from the brand answers
system_fields.source_refs: paths of the answers file and brand file
system_fields.brand: brand_colors, fonts, logo and photos questions

questions.text: How would you like to set this up?
questions.why: It decides how much I suggest and how much I ask.
choices: Set it up for me to review

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Pick the first if you have your answers ready. Pick the second and I will explain each choice. Pick the third and I will suggest everything for you to review before anything is built.

default.reason: Most people want explanations; you can change this any time.

questions.text: What is your business or brand name, exactly as it should appear on your pages?
questions.why: It goes on the page and the checkout, and becomes your logo text if you have no logo file.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Type it the way you want customers to see it, with your capital letters.

questions.text: What is the exact name of your offer, as it should be written on the page?
questions.why: The name is used word for word. I never invent or change it.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: This is the title of what you sell: a course, event, program or service.

questions.text: In a sentence or two, what are you offering, and who is it for? A rough sentence, a link or pasted notes are all fine.
questions.why: The offer and its buyer anchor every later choice, and the claims on the page come only from what you say here.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Say what it is and who it helps. You can paste your own notes.
examples: A 6-week group program that helps new coaches get their first 10 paying clients.

questions.text: Who is this for? Name 3 to 6 kinds of people, and for each one, what do they want?
questions.why: The page speaks to these people directly.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Think of the people who buy from you today. What result do they want, not the steps to get it?
examples: New coaches who want their first paying clients
Busy moms who want to start a side business

questions.text: What will be different for someone after they use it?
questions.why: It is the realistic result the page promises. I will never invent a guarantee.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Finish this sentence: after this, my buyer can ___ within ___.
examples: After 6 weeks you have a clear offer and 3 conversations booked.

questions.text: What are the three biggest problems it solves for them? Short phrases are fine.
questions.why: The page is built around three distinct problems.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: One about their day-to-day, one about how they privately feel, one about who sees them stuck.
examples: Family asking when they will get a real job

questions.text: What does the buyer actually get? A rough list is fine. Include amounts, access time or dates where you know them.
questions.why: What buyers get is a promise they rely on, so it must be yours.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: List every item: modules, calls, templates, bonuses.

questions.text: Do you have real results, stories or kind words from buyers that we may use? Paste or link them, or say none yet.
questions.why: Proof must be real and credited. If you have none yet, the page is written without it.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A testimonial, a result with a number, or a screenshot you have permission to share.
examples: "I booked 3 clients in 2 weeks." - Dana R.

default.reason: No proof is invented; the page is written without a proof section.

questions.text: Tell me your story in three short parts: one low moment from your own struggle, the moment you decided things would change, and who you built this for.
questions.why: The personal letter on the page is your real story.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A scene, not a summary. Where were you standing, what did you feel?

questions.text: How do you talk? Give me 2 or 3 words, or paste a paragraph you wrote that sounds like you.
questions.why: The copy is written in your voice.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Words like warm, direct, funny, calm, bold.

default.reason: A neutral friendly voice until you give your own.

questions.text: Who should appear in the images, and how should the people break down? Give percentages, or say no people at all.
questions.why: I never assume who appears in your images.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Say who your buyers are and who you want shown. It can be anyone, including no people.

questions.text: Will buyers choose one offer, a few packages, or levels that build on each other?
questions.why: It decides whether you need a page where buyers choose, and how many pages the funnel has.
choices: Levels that build on each other

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: One offer: everyone buys the same thing. A few packages: buyers pick one (like Basic or Premium). Levels: each higher level includes the one below it.
examples: Levels: Level 1, 2 and 3, each adding more

questions.text: Tell me each package or level on its own line: its name, what is in it, and its price. For example: Premium | 12 lessons; 4 live calls | $497
questions.why: A page where buyers choose, or levels, is built only from packages you name and price. I never invent them.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Give at least two. Each one needs a name and a price; list what is included after the name.

questions.text: Do you already have a price for it, or should I suggest a starting price for you to review?
questions.why: A price is a promise to your buyer. I only use a price you gave or a suggestion you approved.
choices: Suggest one for me to review

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Think about what the result is worth to the buyer, and what similar programs charge. I can suggest a range with my reasoning, but you approve it.

questions.text: How do buyers pay: all at once, monthly, or in parts?
questions.why: The payment plan changes what the checkout shows.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: All at once is one payment. Monthly repeats. In parts splits one price into a few payments.

default.reason: The simplest checkout until you choose.

questions.text: How big do you want this funnel: 3-step, 5-step or 7-step?
questions.why: It sets how many extra offers you build.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: 3-step: page, one upsell, thank-you. 5-step adds a smaller-yes offer and a second upsell. 7-step is the full set: checkout, two upsells, two smaller-yes offers, thank-you.

questions.text: Would a small extra item help them use what they are buying? It appears as an optional add-on before they pay.
questions.why: It is optional on the checkout and starts unchecked.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A small, low-priced extra, like a checklist or a bonus session.

default.reason: No add-on is built until you name one.

questions.text: After they buy, is there a useful upgrade or extra product you want to offer?
questions.why: Upsell 1 adds value on top of the purchase.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Something that helps them get the result faster or go further.

default.reason: No upsell is built until you name one.

questions.text: If they pass on that upgrade, is there a smaller version or an easier way to buy it?
questions.why: A smaller yes keeps a buyer who is not ready for the big one.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A lighter version or split payments.

default.reason: No downsell is built until you name one.

questions.text: After someone takes the upgrade or the smaller offer, should we offer one more helpful product?
questions.why: Upsell 2 is one more optional step.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A bigger or faster option, like done-for-you or a VIP day.

default.reason: No second upsell is built until you name one.

questions.text: If they pass on the second upsell, what is the smallest true yes you can offer?
questions.why: A last smaller offer keeps buyers who are not ready.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A starter tier, one seat, or recordings only.

default.reason: No second downsell is built until you name one.

questions.text: Which pages should I build?
questions.why: Every page you build gets desktop and phone sketches and designs.
choices: Only the main page and checkout

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: The pages are: opt-in page, sales page, page where buyers choose, checkout, upsell, smaller-offer page, and thank-you. The recommended set builds all the ones your funnel uses.
examples: Recommended: landing, sales, checkout, upsells, thank-you

default.reason: The full recommended set for your funnel shape.

questions.text: What are your brand colors? Send color codes like #1A2B3C, or color names. If you have a logo or a website, I can read the colors from it.
questions.why: Every sketch and design is made only in your own colors.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Brand colors are the 2 to 4 colors on your logo, website or business cards. A color code is the # followed by six letters and numbers.

default.reason: A neutral palette that belongs to no client, used until you send your own.

questions.text: Which of these is your MAIN color: the one people think of first when they think of your brand? {colors}
questions.why: The main color is used for buttons and key headlines.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: If you are unsure, pick the color that is most on your logo, or the one you use for buttons on your website.

default.reason: Your first color is used as main until you pick.

questions.text: Which color is your SECOND color, the one that supports the main color? {colors}
questions.why: It is used for section backgrounds and supporting shapes.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: The second color is usually softer or darker than the main color.

default.reason: Your next color is used until you pick.

questions.text: Which color should be the small highlight color for badges and underlines? {colors}
questions.why: An accent adds a little spark. The other colors stay as extras.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Pick the brightest of what is left, or choose none.

default.reason: The next color is used as the highlight until you pick.

questions.text: What should the page background be?
questions.why: Text has to be easy to read on it.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Light backgrounds feel open and clean. Dark backgrounds feel premium and dramatic. Most coaching pages use light.

default.reason: Light is the easiest to read.

questions.text: Do you have a logo file we can use?
questions.why: Your real logo is used as is. I never redraw it.
choices: Use my business name as text

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A logo file is a PNG or SVG of your logo. If you have none, your business name is set in clean type as a text logo.

default.reason: Your business name is shown as a text logo until you send a file.

questions.text: Do you have brand fonts, the typefaces on your logo or website?
questions.why: Fonts give the page its personality.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A font is the shape of the letters. If you do not know, I pick a pair that suits your brand and show you.
examples: Playfair Display for headlines, Source Sans 3 for text

default.reason: Fonts are chosen to suit your brand and shown to you to confirm.

questions.text: Do you want a real photo of you on the page? If yes, send one or two clear photos.
questions.why: Real people build trust. I never generate a lookalike of you.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A clear, well-lit photo of your face works best. If you send none, the page has an empty photo frame you can fill later.

default.reason: An empty photo frame is used; no likeness is generated.

questions.text: Do you give us permission to use the photos you send on your page and ads for this launch?
questions.why: I only use photos of people with their permission.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: This covers photos of you and anyone in them. You can withdraw it any time.

default.reason: Without a clear yes, your photos are not used.

questions.text: Which look do you want for your page: A, B or C?
questions.why: The style sets the shape of the photos and sections.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A Block: clean rectangles, classic and polished. B Circle: round photos with colored rings, warm and friendly. C Hybrid: Block structure with round photos only for personal pictures. If you are unsure, tell me three words for how you want your brand to feel.

default.reason: Block is the most neutral look.

questions.text: Optional: do you have a registered design style card id (it starts with FN-)? Leave blank if not.
questions.why: It locks every image to that style.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Only if you were given one. Most people skip this.

questions.text: Which image service should make your pictures?
questions.why: I only name a service after checking it works for you.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: This is the service that draws the pictures. If you are not sure, I use the one already connected to your account.

default.reason: The standard connected image service.

questions.text: What is the most pictures I should make for this launch?
questions.why: It is a ceiling, not a purchase. Paid pictures also need your separate OK.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Each page needs a handful of pictures. 12 covers a small funnel, 24 a full one.

default.reason: A modest ceiling; raising it needs your OK.

questions.text: Do you approve spending on paid pictures, and what is the most you want to spend?
questions.why: Paid work needs its own OK, separate from approving the plan.
choices: Yes, up to a limit I will give

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Nothing paid is made until you say yes with an amount. Sketches and free drafts do not cost anything.

questions.text: Should the main page be the standard length, or the long, detailed version?
questions.why: Length is your choice.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Standard is shorter and quicker to read. Long-form tells more of the story and suits bigger prices.

default.reason: Standard length until you choose.

questions.text: Should this go into your existing Convert & Flow account?
questions.why: The account is checked from your own access, never typed in.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: If you already use Convert & Flow, choose yes.

questions.text: I need three real facts: your community link, what the bonus is, and a yes that you will really send the personal text.
questions.why: The pages only promise what you will do.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Give the real community URL, name the bonus, and confirm you will send the text.
examples: https://example.com/community; Bonus: planner PDF; text confirmed: yes

questions.text: Is this launch kit included in what you bought or have a license for?
questions.why: A launch is only built with a confirmed right to run it.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: I check this against your account record. I never assume it.

questions.text: Here is the plan I recommend. Do you approve it for building, or would you like a change?
questions.why: Approval is tied to the exact plan you saw.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Nothing is built until you approve.
